Apple___Apple_scab.Symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on apple leaves and fruit, causing premature leaf drop.
Apple___Apple_scab.Cause: Venturia inaequalis fungus favored by cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.Biological Treatment: Spray Bacillus subtilis or Serenade ASO @ 5g/L during bud break.
Apple___Apple_scab.Chemical Treatment: Apply Captan 50% WP @ 2.5g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L water.
Apple___Apple_scab.Organic Recommendation: Spray sulfur 80% WDG (3g/L) or copper soap fungicide at first sign of green tip.
Apple___Apple_scab.Prevention Tips: Rake and burn fallen infected apple leaves in autumn to destroy overwintering spores.
Apple___Apple_scab.Immediate Precautions: Improve canopy pruning to increase air movement and sunlight penetration.
Apple___Apple_scab.Future Prevention: Plant scab-resistant apple cultivars like Liberty, Freedom, or Enterprise.
Apple___Apple_scab.Recovery Advice: Foliage recovery expected in 10-14 days following fungicide application.

Apple___Black_rot.Symptoms: Purple spots on leaves expanding to frog-eye leaf spots; reddish-brown decay on fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.Cause: Botryosphaeria obtusa fungus invading pruning wounds and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.Biological Treatment: Apply Trichoderma harzianum as protective foliar spray.
Apple___Black_rot.Organic Recommendation: Apply Liquid Copper Fungicide (2.5mL/L) early in the morning.
Apple___Black_rot.Prevention Tips: Remove all mummified apples and dead wood during winter pruning.
Apple___Black_rot.Immediate Precautions: Prune out infected twigs at least 15cm below visible symptoms.
Apple___Black_rot.Future Prevention: Maintain orchard sanitation and burn prunings immediately.
Apple___Black_rot.Recovery Advice: New leaf growth remains clean after sanitation and spray treatment.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on upper leaf surface with tube-like spore structures beneath.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Cause: Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae rust fungus requiring nearby cedar/juniper hosts.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Biological Treatment: Apply Neem oil 3% extract every 7-10 days during rainy spring periods.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Chemical Treatment: Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Organic Recommendation: Apply Wettable Sulfur @ 3g/L at blossom pink stage.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Prevention Tips: Remove Eastern red cedar trees within 1-2 miles of the orchard if feasible.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Immediate Precautions: Apply preventative fungicide prior to expected spring rain events.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Future Prevention: Plant rust-resistant apple varieties like Red Free or William's Pride.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.Recovery Advice: Orange leaf spots stabilize within 7-10 days after treatment.

Apple___healthy.Symptoms: Vibrant green leaves without spots, discoloration, or structural distortion.
Apple___healthy.Cause: Optimal orchard management, balanced nutrition, and dry foliage conditions.
Apple___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply preventative bio-stimulants or bio-protectants once every 14 days.
Apple___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Maintain foliar health with seaweed extract (2mL/L) and organic compost wash.
Apple___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain clean orchard floor and proper drip irrigation schedule.
Apple___healthy.Future Prevention: Continue seasonal dormant oil sprays for scale and mite prevention.
Apple___healthy.Recovery Advice: Trees are in peak healthy state.

Blueberry___healthy.Symptoms: Uniform green foliage, firm stems, and normal berry cluster development.
Blueberry___healthy.Cause: Well-drained acidic soil (pH 4.5-5.5) and appropriate mulch cover.
Blueberry___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply Mycorrhizal root inoculants during early season fertigation.
Blueberry___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Apply pine bark mulch and elemental sulfur to preserve soil acidity.
Blueberry___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain soil moisture with drip irrigation.
Blueberry___healthy.Recovery Advice: Blueberry crop is healthy and flourishing.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Symptoms: White powdery fungal coating on leaves and young shoots causing curling.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Cause: Podosphaera clandestina fungus spreading in warm, dry weather with high humidity.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus subtilis (3g/L).
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Chemical Treatment: Apply Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1mL/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5mL/L.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Organic Recommendation: Spray potassium bicarbonate (5g/L) or neem oil 3% at first symptom.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Prevention Tips: Prune tree center to allow airflow and sun exposure.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Immediate Precautions: Avoid overhead irrigation during evening hours.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Future Prevention: Apply early season sulfur sprays before dense canopy closure.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.Recovery Advice: Powdery mildew washes off and leaves uncurl in 7-10 days.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Symptoms: Deep green, glossy foliage without leaf spots or white fungal patches.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Cause: Good canopy aeration and balanced fertigation.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Spray compost tea or vermicompost extract.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Protect foliage from severe wind damage.
Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.Future Prevention: Conduct annual winter pruning for optimal structure.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Symptoms: Rectangular grey-to-tan lesions constrained by leaf veins on lower leaves.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Cause: Cercospora zeae-maydis fungus favored by high humidity and zero-till crop residues.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Chemical Treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1mL/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Organic Recommendation: Spray copper oxychloride (3g/L) combined with neem kernel extract.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Prevention Tips: Rotate maize field with non-host crops like soybean or peanut for 2 years.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Immediate Precautions: Plow under or shred crop residues after harvest to reduce spore carryover.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Future Prevention: Select high-yielding grey leaf spot resistant maize hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.Recovery Advice: Lesion expansion ceases within 7 days of systemic fungicide spray.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Symptoms: Small powdery brownish-red pustules scattered on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Cause: Puccinia sorghi fungus spread via windborne spores in cool humid air.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Chemical Treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1mL/L.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 3% + garlic extract solution.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Prevention Tips: Plant early in the season and use disease-resistant hybrids.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Future Prevention: Rotate maize with legumes or soybean.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.Recovery Advice: Pustules dry up and rust spread stops in 7-10 days.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Symptoms: Long elliptical grayish-green cigar-shaped lesions expanding across leaf blades.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Cause: Exserohilum turcicum fungus thriving under moist conditions and moderate temp (18-27°C).
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply liquid copper soap (2.5mL/L) at silking stage.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Prevention Tips: Manage crop residues and rotate with soybean or pulses.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Immediate Precautions: Monitor field during humid post-rain periods.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Future Prevention: Choose resistant corn hybrids with Ht resistance genes.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.Recovery Advice: Blight spot spread halted within 7 days.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.Symptoms: Sturdy green leaves without lesions, striping, or fungal rust pustules.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Cause: Adequate NPK nutrition and proper crop rotation.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply PSB (Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria) to roots.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Apply vermicompost and liquid humic acid.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain optimum plant population and inter-row spacing.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Future Prevention: Soil testing prior to next planting season.
Corn_(maize)___healthy.Recovery Advice: Maize crop is in excellent health.

Grape___Black_rot.Symptoms: Small reddish-brown spots on leaves; dark shriveled black mummy berries on clusters.
Grape___Black_rot.Cause: Guignardia bidwellii fungus surviving in infected black mummy berries.
Grape___Black_rot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Grape___Black_rot.Organic Recommendation: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L before rainy spells.
Grape___Black_rot.Prevention Tips: Destroy all mummified grape clusters and pruned canes during winter.
Grape___Black_rot.Immediate Precautions: Tuck shoots to ensure good sun exposure and fast canopy drying.
Grape___Black_rot.Future Prevention: Establish vine trellising for optimal ventilation.
Grape___Black_rot.Recovery Advice: Foliar black rot spots dry out in 7-10 days.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Symptoms: Tiger-stripe yellow/brown leaf chlorosis; dark purple spots on fruit skins.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Cause: Complex of wood-rotting fungi (Phaeomoniella, Phaeoacremonium, Fomitiporia).
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Biological Treatment: Protect pruning wounds with Trichoderma viride paste.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Chemical Treatment: No effective chemical cure; paint large cuts with wound sealant.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Organic Recommendation: Soil drench with bio-fungicides and compost tea.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Prevention Tips: Prune vines during dry weather to prevent spore entry into wood wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Immediate Precautions: Mark infected vines and prune them last to avoid tool contamination.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Future Prevention: Replace severely declining vines with healthy certified stock.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).Recovery Advice: Manage vine stress to prolong productivity.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Symptoms: Irregular dark brown leaf spots with yellow halos, leading to leaf drop.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Chemical Treatment: Spray Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Organic Recommendation: Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Neem oil 3%.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Prevention Tips: Remove and burn fallen infected leaf debris after harvest.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.Future Prevention: Maintain balanced potassium and nitrogen supply.

Grape___healthy.Symptoms: Lush dark green vine foliage and healthy berry clusters without spots.
Grape___healthy.Cause: Balanced canopy management and timely spray schedule.
Grape___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Foliar feed with seaweed extract and liquid potash.
Grape___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Protect vines from mechanical fruit injury.
Grape___healthy.Recovery Advice: Vineyard foliage is in prime condition.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Symptoms: Asymmetrical yellow mottling on leaves, stunted small green sour fruit with dark seeds.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Cause: Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus bacteria transmitted by Asian citrus psyllid insect vector.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Biological Treatment: Control Asian citrus psyllid vectors using Chrysoperla carnea predators.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Chemical Treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5mL/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L to kill psyllids.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 5% + insecticidal soap to manage psyllid populations.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Prevention Tips: Plant only certified disease-free citrus saplings from accredited nurseries.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Immediate Precautions: Remove severely infected trees to prevent orchard-wide transmission.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Future Prevention: Implement strict psyllid monitor traps and regional management.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).Recovery Advice: Maintain nutritional sprays (Zn, Fe, Mn) to support affected trees.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.Symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots turning dark brown-purple, eventually dropping out (shot-hole).
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Cause: Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni bacteria spread by wind-blown rain.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Biological Treatment: Apply Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L during early leaf push.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Chemical Treatment: Apply Oxytetracycline or Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 1.5g/L at dormant/pink stage.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Organic Recommendation: Low-rate Copper Octanoate spray (1.5mL/L) during early vegetative growth.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Prevention Tips: Avoid planting susceptible peach varieties in high-wind, wet locations.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Immediate Precautions: Do not spray high-concentration copper during green leafing to avoid phytotoxicity.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Future Prevention: Select bacterial spot resistant peach cultivars like Candor or Sentinel.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.Recovery Advice: Shot-hole leaf drop stabilizes after copper treatment.

Peach___healthy.Symptoms: Smooth green foliage, vibrant bark, and clean fruit skin.
Peach___healthy.Cause: Optimal orchard aeration and balanced micro-nutrient management.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Symptoms: Small yellow-green leaf spots growing into dark raised water-soaked lesions with yellow halos.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Cause: Xanthomonas euvesicatoria bacteria favored by warm, humid rainy weather.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L water.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Organic Recommendation: Apply copper octanoate (2mL/L) combined with neem oil.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Prevention Tips: Use certified disease-free pepper seeds and avoid overhead irrigation.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Immediate Precautions: Sanitize equipment and shears before moving between fields.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Future Prevention: Practice 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.Recovery Advice: Bacterial lesion spread halted within 7 days.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.Symptoms: Uniform green pepper leaves and firm fruits without spots or wilting.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Cause: Proper soil drainage, balanced NPK fertigation, and pest control.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray with panchagavya 3% or vermiwash.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Prevention Tips: Mulch soil around plants to retain moisture.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Monitor for early thrips or aphid vectors.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Future Prevention: Maintain soil health and crop rotation.
Pepper,_bell___healthy.Recovery Advice: Bell pepper plants are in great condition.

Potato___Early_blight.Symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric target-like rings on lower mature potato leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.Cause: Alternaria solani fungus surviving in infected tubers and soil debris.
Potato___Early_blight.Biological Treatment: Spray Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/L or Bacillus subtilis @ 3g/L.
Potato___Early_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L.
Potato___Early_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) or Copper Oxychloride 3g/L.
Potato___Early_blight.Prevention Tips: Maintain high soil fertility with adequate potassium and nitrogen.
Potato___Early_blight.Immediate Precautions: Remove and burn lower infected leaves; hill potato rows high.
Potato___Early_blight.Future Prevention: Use 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Potato___Early_blight.Recovery Advice: Leaf spotting stops spreading within 7-10 days.

Potato___Late_blight.Symptoms: Large dark brown-black water-soaked lesions on leaf tips/edges with white mold underneath.
Potato___Late_blight.Cause: Phytophthora infestans oomycete pathogen thriving in cool, wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.Biological Treatment: Pre-treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L soil drenching.
Potato___Late_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g/L.
Potato___Late_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or liquid copper soap.
Potato___Late_blight.Prevention Tips: Plant certified disease-free seed tubers and hill soil high over developing tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.Immediate Precautions: Destroy heavily infected foliage 2 weeks prior to harvest to protect tubers.
Potato___Late_blight.Recovery Advice: Re-check field in 5 days after systemic fungicide application.

Potato___healthy.Symptoms: Lush green potato foliage and sturdy stems free of lesions.
Potato___healthy.Cause: Certified clean seed tubers, ideal soil moisture, and good hilling.
Potato___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Foliar feed with Panchagavya 3% or neem spray.
Potato___healthy.Prevention Tips: Keep ridges well-hilled to prevent tuber exposure.
Potato___healthy.Recovery Advice: Potato crop is healthy and vigorous.

Raspberry___healthy.Symptoms: Bright green leaves, clean canes, and normal flower/fruit clusters.
Raspberry___healthy.Cause: Good row spacing, drip irrigation, and cane pruning.
Raspberry___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis for early caterpillars if needed.
Raspberry___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Mulch row beds with wood chips or straw.
Raspberry___healthy.Prevention Tips: Prune out spent floricanes immediately after harvest.
Raspberry___healthy.Future Prevention: Maintain wide row spacing for sunlight.

Soybean___healthy.Symptoms: Uniform green trifoliate leaves without yellowing, rust, or bacterial spots.
Soybean___healthy.Cause: Rhizobium nodulation, adequate rainfall, and insect management.
Soybean___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Foliar application of liquid humic acid and micronutrient zinc.
Soybean___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain optimum seed depth and field drainage.
Soybean___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Avoid field access when leaves are wet.
Soybean___healthy.Future Prevention: Rotate soybean with corn or wheat.
Soybean___healthy.Recovery Advice: Soybean field is in peak condition.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.Symptoms: Dusty white powdery coating covering upper leaf surfaces, turning leaves yellow and brittle.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Cause: Podosphaera xanthii fungus spreading rapidly under high humidity and warm shade.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus subtilis (3g/L).
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Chemical Treatment: Apply Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1mL/L.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Organic Recommendation: Spray potassium bicarbonate (5g/L) or 10% cow milk solution.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Prevention Tips: Plant squash in full sunlight with adequate spacing for air circulation.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Immediate Precautions: Remove severely infected older leaves at base of plant.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Future Prevention: Select PM-resistant squash and pumpkin hybrids.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.Recovery Advice: Powdery mildew washes off and new leaves remain green in 7 days.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Symptoms: Irregular purple-red spots with dark brown centers on leaves, causing scorched dry leaf edges.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Cause: Diplocarpon earlianum fungus favored by wet conditions and overhead watering.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Chemical Treatment: Apply Captan 50% WP @ 2.5g/L or Myclobutanil 10% WP @ 1g/L.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Organic Recommendation: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or neem seed oil (3%).
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Prevention Tips: Use straw mulch around plants to prevent leaf contact with wet soil.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Immediate Precautions: Remove old infected leaves during post-harvest renovation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Future Prevention: Switch from overhead sprinklers to drip irrigation.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.Recovery Advice: New strawberry runner leaves emerge healthy within 10 days.

Strawberry___healthy.Symptoms: Dark green trifoliate leaves, healthy white blooms, and clean runner crowns.
Strawberry___healthy.Cause: Adequate drip fertigation and proper mulching.
Strawberry___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Spray vermicompost wash and organic potassium.
Strawberry___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Prevent fruit resting directly on damp soil.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Symptoms: Small dark brown water-soaked leaf spots with yellow halos, leading to defoliation.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Cause: Xanthomonas vesicatoria bacteria spread by rain splash and contaminated seeds.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Biological Treatment: Spray Bacillus subtilis @ 3g/L or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Organic Recommendation: Apply copper soap (2mL/L) mixed with neem oil.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Prevention Tips: Treat seeds with hot water or sodium hypochlorite before sowing.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Immediate Precautions: Prune bottom foliage and avoid handling plants when wet.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Future Prevention: Maintain 2-3 year crop rotation away from solanaceous crops.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.Recovery Advice: Bacterial spot spread stops within 7 days.

Tomato___Early_blight.Symptoms: Dark brown concentric target-like rings on mature lower leaves with yellow halos.
Tomato___Early_blight.Cause: Alternaria solani fungal spores spread via wind, splashing rain, and residues.
Tomato___Early_blight.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis (2g/L) or Trichoderma harzianum (5g/L).
Tomato___Early_blight.Chemical Treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Tomato___Early_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply copper oxychloride (3g/L) mixed with 1% milk solution or neem oil.
Tomato___Early_blight.Prevention Tips: Mulch soil around base with straw to stop soil splash.
Tomato___Early_blight.Immediate Precautions: Prune and burn infected bottom leaves immediately.
Tomato___Early_blight.Future Prevention: Plant resistant hybrids and maintain strict Solanaceae crop rotation.

Tomato___Late_blight.Symptoms: Large water-soaked dark green-black lesions on leaves and stems with white mold.
Tomato___Late_blight.Cause: Phytophthora infestans oomycete pathogen thriving in cool, wet, humid weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.Biological Treatment: Pre-treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens (10g/L) soil drenching.
Tomato___Late_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g/L.
Tomato___Late_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L.
Tomato___Late_blight.Prevention Tips: Ensure high-ridge planting for efficient drainage.
Tomato___Late_blight.Immediate Precautions: Isolate affected field patch; avoid morning harvesting.
Tomato___Late_blight.Future Prevention: Use certified late-blight resistant tomato cultivars.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Symptoms: Pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface with velvety olive-green fungal mold underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Cause: Passalora fulva (Cladosporium fulvum) fungus thriving in high humidity (>85%) and poor ventilation.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Chemical Treatment: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5mL/L.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Organic Recommendation: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or liquid sulfur spray.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Prevention Tips: Increase greenhouse ventilation and lower indoor relative humidity below 85%.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Immediate Precautions: Prune overcrowded lower branches to promote air movement.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Future Prevention: Select leaf mold resistant tomato varieties (Cf-9 gene).
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.Recovery Advice: Fungal velvety growth dries up in 7-10 days.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Symptoms: Numerous small circular spots with dark brown margins and greyish centers containing tiny black dots.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Cause: Septoria lycopersici fungus spread by rain splash and field tools.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Chemical Treatment: Apply Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Organic Recommendation: Spray 1% Bordeaux mixture or Neem seed kernel extract (5%).
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Prevention Tips: Mulch heavy around tomato roots and use drip irrigation.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Immediate Precautions: Remove lower infected leaves before spots reach upper canopy.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Future Prevention: Rotate away from tomatoes, potatoes, and eggplant for 2 years.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.Recovery Advice: Septoria spot expansion halts in 7 days.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Symptoms: Fine yellow speckling/bronzing on upper leaves with delicate silk webbing underneath.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Cause: Tetranychus urticae mites multiplying rapidly in hot, dry, dusty conditions.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Biological Treatment: Release predatory mites (Phytoseiulus persimilis) or Chrysoperla carnea.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Chemical Treatment: Spray Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1mL/L or Abamectin 1.9% EC @ 0.5mL/L.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 3% + insecticidal potassium soap (5mL/L) on leaf undersides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Prevention Tips: Keep field perimeters wet and dust-free to discourage spider mite buildup.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Immediate Precautions: Direct spray nozzles thoroughly at undersides of leaves.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Future Prevention: Avoid over-application of synthetic pyrethroid insecticides.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.Recovery Advice: New leaf growth emerges un-speckled within 5-7 days.

Tomato___Target_Spot.Symptoms: Small water-soaked leaf spots expanding into brown lesions with faint concentric rings.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Cause: Corynespora cassiicola fungus favored by warm temperatures (20-30°C) and long dew periods.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Chemical Treatment: Spray Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1mL/L or Pyraclostrobin 20% WG @ 1g/L.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Organic Recommendation: Spray Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L combined with neem oil.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Prevention Tips: Avoid planting near older infected solanaceous crop fields.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Immediate Precautions: Improve plant staking and row aeration.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Future Prevention: Perform field sanitation and turn under crop debris post-harvest.
Tomato___Target_Spot.Recovery Advice: Target spots dry up and stop expanding within 7 days.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Symptoms: Severe upward leaf curling, yellowing leaf margins, stunted plant growth, and flower drop.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Cause: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus (TYLCV) transmitted exclusively by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Biological Treatment: Set up yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre) to catch whiteflies; spray Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5g/L.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Chemical Treatment: Spray Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.5mL/L or Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L to eliminate whitefly vectors.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Organic Recommendation: Spray Neem oil 5% or pongamia oil (5mL/L) every 5 days.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Prevention Tips: Use 40-mesh insect-proof netting over nurseries and young seedling beds.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Immediate Precautions: Rogue out severely stunted virused plants early to reduce vector inoculum.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Future Prevention: Plant TYLCV-resistant tomato hybrids (e.g., Ty-1/Ty-3 gene cultivars).
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.Recovery Advice: Vector control stops virus spread to healthy neighboring plants.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Symptoms: Mottled light and dark green mosaic patterns on leaves, leaf distortion, and fern-like leaves.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Cause: Tomato Mosaic Virus (ToMV) mechanically transmitted via hands, tools, and clothing.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Biological Treatment: Soak seeds in 10% trisodium phosphate (TSP) solution for 30 mins before sowing.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Chemical Treatment: No chemical cure for virus; focus on hygiene and tool sterilization.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray with skimmed milk (10%) to neutralize viral particle transfer.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Prevention Tips: Wash hands with soap and water before handling tomato plants; do not smoke near plants.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.Immediate Precautions: Sanitize pruning shears with 70% alcohol or 10% bleach solution between rows.

Tomato___healthy.Symptoms: No spots or lesions. Stems and foliage are vibrant green and structurally strong.
Tomato___healthy.Cause: Optimal soil moisture, balanced nutrition, and clean field hygiene.
Tomato___healthy.Biological Treatment: Apply Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens as bio-protectants once every 14 days.
Tomato___healthy.Organic Recommendation: Spray neem oil 3% or vermicompost wash to maintain foliar immunity.
Tomato___healthy.Prevention Tips: Maintain 60cm row spacing for adequate sunlight penetration and airflow.
Tomato___healthy.Immediate Precautions: Avoid flood irrigation during high-humidity evenings.
Tomato___healthy.Future Prevention: Practice 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops.
Tomato___healthy.Recovery Advice: Field is in optimal health. Continue standard fertigation.

Rice___Leaf_Blast.Symptoms: Diamond or spindle-shaped lesions with grayish centers and reddish-brown borders on leaf blades.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Cause: Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia oryzae) fungus encouraged by high nitrogen levels and leaf wetness.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Biological Treatment: Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L during early morning.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Chemical Treatment: Apply Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5mL/L water.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Organic Recommendation: Spray Panchagavya 3% or Vermiwash 10% solution combined with Neem oil (3%).
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Prevention Tips: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertigation; split nitrogen into 3-4 applications.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Immediate Precautions: Drain standing water from field for 2-3 days to reduce canopy humidity.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Future Prevention: Cultivate blast-resistant varieties like ADT 43, CO 51, or CR Dhan 305.
Rice___Leaf_Blast.Recovery Advice: Visible suppression of diamond spots expected within 8-10 days.

Rice___Bacterial_blight.Symptoms: Wavy yellow-to-brown wilting stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, progressing downwards.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Cause: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacteria entering leaf hydathodes and root wounds.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Biological Treatment: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed + foliar spray @ 1kg/ha.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Chemical Treatment: Spray Copper Oxychloride 50% WP @ 2.5g/L + Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L water.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Organic Recommendation: Apply Fresh cow dung slurry supernatant (5%) or turmeric powder extract.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Prevention Tips: Drain excess field water and avoid clipping leaf tips during transplanting.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Immediate Precautions: Refrain from excessive top-dressing of urea fertilizer.
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Future Prevention: Grow resistant rice varieties such as Improved Samba Mahsuri (RP Bio-226).
Rice___Bacterial_blight.Recovery Advice: Bacterial spread halts within 5-7 days following copper-streptomycin application.

Rice___Brown_spot.Symptoms: Oval or circular dark brown spots with yellow halos evenly distributed across mature leaf blades.
Rice___Brown_spot.Cause: Bipolaris oryzae fungus associated with nutrient-deficient (potassium & zinc) or drought-stressed soils.
Rice___Brown_spot.Biological Treatment: Soil application of Trichoderma viride @ 2.5kg/ha mixed with 100kg farmyard manure.
Rice___Brown_spot.Chemical Treatment: Apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L.
Rice___Brown_spot.Organic Recommendation: Foliar application of wood ash slurry (5%) and zinc sulfate (0.5%).
Rice___Brown_spot.Prevention Tips: Maintain balanced soil fertility, applying Zinc Sulfate @ 25kg/ha at basal planting.
Rice___Brown_spot.Immediate Precautions: Provide timely irrigation to relieve moisture stress.
Rice___Brown_spot.Future Prevention: Conduct soil test and replenish potassium and organic matter prior to next season.
Rice___Brown_spot.Recovery Advice: Leaf vigor recovers in 10 days upon nutrient replenishment and spray.

Unknown.Symptoms: Unusual leaf discoloration, spotting, or leaf curling.
Unknown.Cause: Pathogen, nutrient imbalance, or environmental stress.
Unknown.Biological Treatment: Apply general bio-fungicide (Trichoderma @ 5g/L) and neem spray.
Unknown.Chemical Treatment: Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agronomist for lab analysis.
Unknown.Organic Recommendation: Improve soil health with vermicompost and balanced micro-nutrients.
Unknown.Prevention Tips: Maintain proper field drainage and crop sanitation.
Unknown.Immediate Precautions: Monitor field daily and capture clear foliar images for re-scan.
Unknown.Future Prevention: Conduct soil and water quality testing.
Unknown.Recovery Advice: Re-assess plant health score in 5 days.

Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins that rapidly turn yellow to white, wilting young seedlings (kresek).
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Cause: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacteria spread through rain, wind, and irrigation water.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Immediate Precautions: Drain excess standing water from the field and avoid high nitrogen top-dressing.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Prevention Tips: Use resistant rice varieties, maintain balanced soil nutrition, and burn infected crop stubble.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Organic Recommendation: Spray Fresh Neem Kernel Extract 5% or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/L.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Chemical Treatment: Apply Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L combined with Copper Oxychloride 3g/L.
Rice___Bacterial_leaf_blight.Recovery Advice: Lesion expansion slows down and new tillers show healthy green foliage within 10-12 days.

Rice___Leaf_smut.symptoms: Small, slightly raised black linear spots scattered on leaf blades that rupture to release dark spores.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Cause: Entyloma oryzae fungus favored by high nitrogen fertilization and damp weather.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Immediate Precautions: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization and avoid flooding rice paddies.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Prevention Tips: Rotate crops seasonally, balance N-P-K fertilizer applications, and remove field weeds.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Organic Recommendation: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5g/L or neem oil 3% solution.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Chemical Treatment: Apply Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1mL/L or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L.
Rice___Leaf_smut.Recovery Advice: Infection stabilizes and fresh leaves emerge clean within 7-10 days.
